differences.title: 1. DATA TYPES
differences.leftDesc: Offers advanced types like JSONB, arrays, and custom types for complex data.
differences.rightDesc: Supports a wide range of standard SQL data types, well-tested and reliable.

differences.title: 2. EXTENSIBILITY
differences.leftDesc: Supports custom functions, operators, data types, and procedural languages like PL/pgSQL.
differences.rightDesc: Has a good range of plugins and extensions, but less flexible than PostgreSQL.

differences.title: 3. CONCURRENCY CONTROL
differences.leftDesc: Uses Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) for high concurrency with less locking.
differences.rightDesc: Also employs MVCC, but can sometimes encounter more locking issues under heavy load.

differences.title: 4. JSON SUPPORT
differences.leftDesc: Excellent native support for JSONB, offering efficient indexing and querying.
differences.rightDesc: Supports JSON data type, but lacks the performance and indexing of JSONB.

differences.title: 5. REPLICATION
differences.leftDesc: Offers built-in streaming replication (physical & logical) and various third-party solutions.
differences.rightDesc: Provides robust master-slave replication, with semi-sync and group replication available.

differences.title: 6. COMMUNITY & ECOSYSTEM
differences.leftDesc: Vibrant, active community with a focus on open standards and extensibility.
differences.rightDesc: Largest user base, extensive documentation, and wide industry adoption.

differences.title: 7. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Excels with complex queries, large datasets, and high concurrency writes.
differences.rightDesc: Generally performs very well for read-heavy applications and simpler queries.
